content: Each interaction is described in detail, maintaining the original specificity and context. 1. Famotidine and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase the effects or levels of OCT2 substrates. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Calcium Carbonate and Isoniazid: Calcium carbonate reduces isoniazid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 3. Isoniazid and Calcium Carbonate: Isoniazid decreases calcium carbonate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Isotretinoin and Calcium Carbonate: Isotretinoin increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 5. Calcium Carbonate and Isradipine: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of isradipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 6. Calcium Carbonate and Itraconazole: Calcium carbonate decreases itraconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 7. Famotidine and Itraconazole: Famotidine reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Calcium Carbonate and Ketoconazole: Calcium carbonate decreases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Famotidine and Ketoconazole: Famotidine reduces ketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Calcium Carbonate and Labetalol: Calcium carbonate decreases labetalol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor therapy. 11. Calcium Carbonate and Lactulose: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of lactulose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 12. Lanthanum Carbonate and Antacids: Lanthanum carbonate binds cations in the GI tract, potentially reducing the absorption of antacids. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum carbonate. Monitor therapy closely. 13. Calcium Carbonate and Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Calcium carbonate decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to pH-dependent solubility. Use caution and monitor therapy. 14. Famotidine and Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Famotidine reduces ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer famotidine simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at doses not exceeding 40 mg twice daily. Monitor therapy closely. 15. Magnesium Hydroxide and Levofloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases levofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor therapy. 16. Calcium Carbonate and Levofloxacin: Calcium carbonate reduces levofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor therapy. 17. Calcium Carbonate and Levothyroxine: Calcium carbonate decreases levothyroxine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 4 hours and monitor therapy. 18. Calcium Carbonate and Lily of the Valley: Calcium carbonate may increase the effects of lily of the valley through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 19. Calcium Carbonate and Lisdexamfetamine: Calcium carbonate increases lisdexamfetamine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Calcium Carbonate and Lisinopril: Calcium carbonate reduces lisinopril effects through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 21. Calcium Carbonate and Manganese: Calcium carbonate and manganese may mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor therapy. 22. Mannitol and Magnesium Hydroxide: Mannitol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 23. Mefloquine and Famotidine: Mefloquine increases famotidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Calcium Carbonate and Memantine: Calcium carbonate increases memantine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine. Use caution and monitor therapy. 25. Famotidine and Mesalamine: Famotidine reduces mesalamine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor therapy closely. 26. Calcium Carbonate and Mesalamine: Calcium carbonate may alter mesalamine levels through pH-dependent renal tubular reabsorption. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 27. Mestranol and Magnesium Hydroxide: Mestranol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 28. Famotidine and Metformin: Famotidine increases metformin levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 29. Calcium Carbonate and Methscopolamine: Calcium carbonate decreases methscopolamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Methyclothiazide and Calcium Carbonate: Methyclothiazide increases calcium carbonate levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 31. Methyclothiazide and Magnesium Hydroxide: Methyclothiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 32. Famotidine and Methylphenidate: Famotidine reduces methylphenidate effects by altering pH-dependent GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Calcium Carbonate and Methylprednisolone: Methylprednisolone decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 34. Metolazone and Magnesium Hydroxide: Metolazone decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 35. Metolazone and Calcium Carbonate: Metolazone increases calcium carbonate levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to alkalosis or hypercalcemia. Monitor therapy closely. 36. Calcium Carbonate and Metoprolol: Calcium carbonate decreases metoprolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor therapy. 37. Calcium Carbonate and Mexiletine: Calcium carbonate increases mexiletine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine. Use caution and monitor therapy. 38. Famotidine and Mifepristone: Famotidine and mifepristone may mutually increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 39. Magnesium Hydroxide and Minocycline: Magnesium hydroxide decreases minocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Calcium Carbonate and Minocycline: Calcium carbonate decreases minocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
